newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy union chief wants clear govt welfare stand.
newsitem.headline: Italy union chief wants clear govt welfare stand.

text.p: The leader of Italy's largest trade unions group, Sergio Cofferati, said on Wednesday he would not discuss welfare reform with the government until it had finalised its position.

"The government majority will have to agree on the time, the method and the content (of welfare reform) and then we will meet for a discussion," Cofferati, leader of the CGIL labour confederation, told reporters.
"That (talks) is not understandable now in so far as the climate to discuss such delicate issues does not exist," he said.
The centre-left government is trying to reform welfare spending so Italy can meet strict budgetary criteria to join Europe's single currency at its founding in 1999.

It faces resistance from the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, which it relies on for a parliamentary majority, as well as trades unions to plans to bring forward a review of pensions spending to this year from 1998.
